tiers.none: Nothing is claimed. The agent may work, but ORCA says nothing verified about what its policy covers.
tiers.A: Connects and fails closed: for each route, a passing installed receipt for the pinned agent, version and host shows the agent connects and that the uncovered routes listed are refused or asked about.
tiers.B: Approvals validated: for each route, a passing installed receipt for the pinned agent, version and host runs every case the route can run against the real agent.
tiers.C: Execution guard certified: for each route, a passing connected receipt for the pinned agent, version and host from a connected path that proves the route (a live agent, its adapter and ORCA together) runs every case that path can run, and that path excludes no lifecycle or bypass case.

paths.what: ORCA's answer to an ACP session/request_permission ask (resolvePermission, read fresh per ask by acp-session.ts)

excluded.F01: The ask arrives as an ACP request the SDK has already parsed; there are no raw bytes for ORCA to refuse.
excluded.F02: Decided in the session's own process; there is no separate context file to lose.
excluded.F03: Nothing is installed in the agent for this route.
excluded.P02: No raw input or context file on this route (see F01 and F02).
excluded.A04: An ACP ask carries no working directory; the session's directory is fixed when the session opens.

paths.verifies: ORCA's answer to an ask that reaches it, from the policy read at that ask
unverified: That the agent sends an ask for every call it makes
That the agent honours the answer it gets
That events, logs and stored records about the ask are redacted

paths.what: ORCA's Claude Code PreToolUse hook (#704), run as its process runs it (runClaudePreToolHook)

excluded.L08: The hook only hands an ask back to Claude. Whether that ask reaches ORCA's answerer for the same call is unverified until an installed receipt shows it; the answerer cases run on acp-ask.
excluded.F04: The hook never answers allow and offers no options, so there is no option for ORCA to pick on this route.

paths.verifies: The hook program's answer to a PreToolUse frame, with the context ORCA wrote
unverified: That Claude runs the hook on every call, remembered grants included
That a hook ask reaches ORCA as an ACP ask for the same call
That Claude blocks on deny, on a block, on a timeout and when the hook cannot start
That events, logs and stored records about the call are redacted

paths.what: A real Claude Code through the real Claude ACP adapter, in a session opened by ORCA's session factory with the pre-tool hook installed, Claude's own settings allowing every tool, and a model stand-in making each case's tool calls (tools/guard-qualification/connected/)

excluded.F01: The agent builds the hook's input itself; a live run cannot hand the hook malformed bytes. Run on claude-native-hook.
excluded.F02: The session's context file is written by ORCA's factory; damaging it mid-session is a hook-program case. Run on claude-native-hook.
excluded.F03: The installed settings are the factory's own; their shape is checked on claude-native-hook and by the #704 acceptance test.
excluded.F04: The hook offers no options; an ACP ask's option handling is checked on acp-ask, where the options are visible.
excluded.A04: One session has one working directory, fixed when it opens; a live agent cannot make a call from another one.
excluded.P02: No raw input or context file can be damaged from inside a live run (see F01 and F02).

paths.verifies: End to end, for remembered calls Claude would otherwise run unasked: whether each case's call took effect, was asked about through ORCA's human channel, or came back to the model as ORCA's denial or block, judged from the files, the MCP recorder and the tool results
unverified: Behaviour of a real model, which may make calls in shapes the stand-in does not
Agent versions other than the pinned pair; hosts other than linux-x64

Calls Claude Code refuses itself before the hook (a tool it does not offer, an Edit of a missing file, a change to a file it has not read after ORCA denied the read). Nothing runs, but ORCA's decision is unobserved: each is recorded as orcaDecision unobserved and does not count
That events, logs and stored records about the call are redacted

unobserved.F05: Claude Code refuses a tool it does not offer (No such tool available) before any hook runs, so ORCA's decision is never observed. Run as a diagnostic: nothing runs, shown by the request's tool list.
unobserved.A02: The relative Edit (../elsewhere/a.md) is refused by Claude Code (the file does not exist from its working directory) before any hook runs, so that assertion's ORCA decision is unobserved; the case's other calls are observed but cannot stand in for it.
unobserved.B01: Claude Code refuses Edits of ORCA files that do not exist yet, and a change to a file whose read ORCA denied, before any hook runs, so those assertions' ORCA decisions are unobserved; the denied writes in the same case cannot stand in for them.
unobserved.P03: The call to a 4 KB unknown tool name is refused by Claude Code (not offered) before any hook runs, so ORCA's answer for it is unobserved; the other calls' short answers cannot stand in for it.

receipts.note: A receipt is a JSON file committed under tools/guard-qualification/receipts/. It names kind (installed or connected), agent, agentVersion, adapterVersion, host, route, build (the 40-hex ORCA commit it ran), checks.connects, checks.uncoveredRoutesRefused and per-case results, with no case listed twice. It must match the row's pin (agentVersion, adapterVersion, host, build). Tiers are cumulative. These checks are structural only: promotion above none is disabled until a receipt is bound to an independently trusted run. Synthetic receipts never count. A file path or a named residual risk is not proof.
